articles.title: VÍDEO: cliente agride comerciante, sai para buscar arma e volta atirando após vítima se negar a vender produtos de limpeza 'fiado' | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso aconteceu no Paraná. Ninguém se feriu. Homem está sendo procurado pela polícia.
articles.summary: Caso aconteceu no Paraná. Ninguém se feriu. Homem está sendo procurado pela polícia.
articles.body:
Um homem agrediu o dono de uma mercearia, saiu para buscar uma arma e voltou atirando minutos depois no final da tarde deste domingo (15) em Imbituva , nos Campos Gerais do Paraná.

Segundo o comerciante, o ataque de fúria do cliente começou após ele pedir para comprar produtos de limpeza "fiado", ou seja, sem pagar na hora, e ter o pedido negado.

A situação aconteceu no bairro Miraluz e foi filmada por câmeras de segurança. Assista acima.

Cliente agride comerciante, sai buscar arma e volta atirando após vítima se negar a vender produtos de limpeza 'fiado' — Foto: Reprodução

Nas imagens, é possível ver que, durante a discussão, o cliente bate na mesa e dá um tapa no rosto do comerciante, que tenta revidar, mas não o alcança por estar atrás do balcão. Segundo o comerciante, neste momento o cliente disse que retornaria ao estabelecimento para matá-lo.

Eles discutem mais um pouco, o cliente vai embora e volta poucos minutos depois, armado. A esposa do comerciante tranca a porta da mercearia, que é de vidro, mas o homem dá dois tiros e a quebra. Ninguém se feriu.

A mulher sai correndo para dentro em meio aos estilhaços, o homem fica mais alguns instantes discutindo com a arma na mão na frente do estabelecimento e depois vai embora.

O dono da mercadoria disse que, após os tiros, o cliente disse que voltaria novamente.

Ainda de acordo com o comerciante, o cliente já tinha ido à mercadoria no mesmo dia, quando comprou bebidas alcoólicas e pagou normalmente.

A Polícia Militar (PM) foi até o local logo após o ocorrido e procurou pelo homem, mas não o encontrou. Pessoas que estavam na região disseram que ele fugiu em um carro com a ajuda de um familiar.

A Polícia Civil, que está investigando o caso, afirma que já o identificou e continua o procurando, mas optou por não confirmar o nome dele. Até o final da manhã desta segunda-feira (16), ele ainda não tinha sido encontrado.

articles.title: PF faz operação contra segurança clandestina em Belém | G1
articles.standfirst: Durante a 'Operação Parassonia', agentes apreenderam equipamentos e determinaram a substituição dos profissionais por vigilantes regularizados.
articles.summary: Durante a 'Operação Parassonia', agentes apreenderam equipamentos e determinaram a substituição dos profissionais por vigilantes regularizados.
articles.body:
A "Operação Parassonia" fiscalizou sete bares e casas noturnas em Belém — Foto: Divulgação/ Polícia Federal

A Polícia Federal (PF) deflagrou uma operação para combater a atuação de empresas clandestinas de segurança privada em Belém . A "Operação Parassonia" fiscalizou sete bares e casas noturnas na capital paraense, entre os dias 13 e 14 de novembro.

Todos os estabelecimentos vistoriados apresentavam irregularidades na contratação dos serviços de segurança.

De acordo com a PF, tanto as empresas que prestavam o serviço informal quanto os estabelecimentos que as contrataram estão sujeitos a multas que variam de R$ 10 mil a R$ 30 mil.

Os seguranças que estavam irregulares foram retirados dos postos de trabalho, e todo o material de utilizado por eles foi apreendido pela Polícia Federal.

Para que pudessem continuar funcionando, os estabelecimentos foram obrigados a contratar vigilantes de empresas devidamente registradas e autorizadas pela PF.

A legislação vigente proíbe que funcionários contratados para equipe de "apoio" ou "portaria" realizem atividades de segurança. Essa função é exclusiva de vigilantes profissionais, que obrigatoriamente devem ser formados por Escolas de Formação de Profissionais de Segurança Privada credenciadas pela PF.

A Polícia Federal alerta que a contratação de serviços de segurança clandestinos representa um risco aos frequentadores e ao patrimônio dos estabelecimentos, pois esses profissionais não passam por verificação de antecedentes criminais, avaliação de formação, aptidão física ou psicológica.

articles.title: Vereador e esposa são presos após briga com agressões em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: O vereador Joanir Martins (PT), de 51 anos, e a mulher foram presos em flagrante em Amambai. Polícia aponta versões diferentes sobre as agressões.
articles.summary: O vereador Joanir Martins e sua esposa foram presos após briga com foice e agressões em Amambai, mas ganharam liberdade provisória após audiência de custódia.
articles.body:
Vereador Joanir Martins foi preso neste domingo (15) — Foto: Reprodução

O vereador Joanir Martins (PT), de 51 anos, e a esposa foram presos em flagrante após uma briga com agressões e ameaças de morte na Aldeia Limão Verde, em Amambai (MS), no domingo (15). Segundo a Polícia Civil, a mulher teria atacado o marido com objetos e quebrado o para-brisa do carro dele com uma foice. O parlamentar sofreu uma fratura na mão. Os dois foram soltos nesta segunda-feira (16), após audiência de custódia.

Segundo o advogado Anderson Ferreira, que representa Joanir, o vereador não agrediu a esposa e teve a liberdade concedida sem medidas cautelares. Já a mulher recebeu liberdade provisória mediante fiança e medidas cautelares. O nome dela não foi divulgado pela polícia. Após o caso, o Partido dos Trabalhadores (PT) de Amambai divulgou uma nota contra a violência. Leia os posicionamentos da defesa e do partido na íntegra ao final da reportagem.

De acordo com a Polícia Civil, a mulher inicialmente acusou o marido de ameaçá-la de morte e agredi-la com uma foice, causando ferimentos na cabeça, no braço e na perna. No entanto, as duas filhas do casal, que presenciaram a discussão, apresentaram uma versão diferente.

Segundo as testemunhas, a briga começou por ciúmes e suspeitas de infidelidade. Durante a discussão, a mulher teria usado uma foice para quebrar o para-brisa do carro do marido e passado a agredi-lo com outros objetos.

As filhas intervieram para separar o casal. Uma delas, adolescente, teria empurrado a mãe, que caiu e sofreu um ferimento na cabeça.

A Polícia Civil informou que não encontrou elementos suficientes para atribuir ao vereador as lesões denunciadas pela esposa. Já o exame de corpo de delito constatou que ele sofreu uma fratura em um osso da mão direita, considerada lesão corporal grave.

As filhas também relataram episódios anteriores de agressividade da mãe, incluindo uma situação em que ela teria atacado o marido com uma faca, causando ferimentos que exigiram atendimento hospitalar.

Uma das testemunhas afirmou ainda que a mãe costumava dizer que poderia inventar acusações contra o marido por acreditar que a Justiça daria mais credibilidade à palavra dela.

Apesar de não ter sido apontado como responsável pelas lesões da esposa, o vereador foi autuado por ameaça em contexto de violência doméstica, já que as filhas confirmaram que ele fez ameaças de morte durante a discussão.

A mulher foi autuada por denunciação caluniosa, lesão corporal grave, dano qualificado e ameaça. A Polícia Civil pediu a prisão preventiva dela, mas a Justiça concedeu liberdade provisória mediante fiança e medidas cautelares, conforme informou a defesa do vereador.

Segundo o advogado, a decisão que colocou Joanir em liberdade considerou que ele é primário, tem bons antecedentes e que as ameaças ocorreram durante uma discussão em que os dois teriam ameaçado um ao outro.

"A versão do vereador Joanir Martins, confirmada pelas filhas do casal, que presenciaram os fatos, é a de que ele não agrediu a esposa. Foi ele quem sofreu as agressões. Segundo a defesa, após um desentendimento entre o casal, a esposa, nervosa, passou a danificar o carro de Joanir. Com a intervenção das filhas e do marido para contê-la, ela acabou caindo e se machucando. O vereador, por sua vez, sofreu fratura em uma das mãos, constatada no exame de corpo de delito. Essa versão foi acolhida na investigação. A própria Polícia Civil informou que não foram identificados elementos para atribuir ao vereador as lesões inicialmente denunciadas. Nesta segunda-feira, 16 de novembro, a Justiça concedeu liberdade a Joanir Martins sem impor qualquer medida cautelar. A decisão registra que ele é primário, tem bons antecedentes e que a única conduta a ele atribuída, a de ameaça, teria ocorrido em contexto de ameaças recíprocas, depois que a esposa começou a danificar seu veículo. Estamos acompanhando o caso e o vereador responderá em liberdade, com tranquilidade, ao que resta a ser esclarecido."

"O Partido dos Trabalhadores de Amambai reafirma seu compromisso com a defesa da vida, da dignidade humana, do respeito e dos direitos de todas as pessoas. Repudiamos veementemente toda e qualquer forma de violência, seja ela física, psicológica, moral ou de qualquer outra natureza. A violência não pode ser naturalizada, relativizada ou tolerada em nossa sociedade. Acreditamos que o respeito, o diálogo, a responsabilidade e a justiça devem nortear as relações humanas e a atuação de todos aqueles que ocupam espaços públicos e representam a sociedade. Violência jamais será um caminho aceitável. O respeito à vida e à dignidade humana deve estar sempre em primeiro lugar." PT – Partido dos Trabalhadores de Amambai/MS

articles.title: Acidente na Rodovia Castello Branco deixa um morto em Itatinga | G1
articles.standfirst: Gilma Diniz, de 54 anos, foi arremessada para fora do veículo da família e atingida por outros carros que passavam pela rodovia, no domingo (15). O motorista, que era irmão da vítima, perdeu o controle após o pneu estourar.
articles.summary: Colisão ocorreu na noite de domingo (15) em Itatinga; nove pessoas foram socorridas em estado grave após capotamento seguido de batida na pista sentido capital.
articles.body:
Mulher de 54 anos morre após ser arremessada para fora do carro e ser atropelada por outros veículos na SP-280, em Itatinga (SP) — Foto: Portal CCM — ARTESP (ccm.artesp.sp.gov.br)

Uma mulher de 54 anos morreu após ser arremessada para fora do carro em que estava e ser atropelada por outros veículos na Rodovia Castello Branco (SP-280), em Itatinga (SP), na noite de domingo (15).

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, a vítima, Gilma Diniz, viajava em um carro, acompanhada pelo irmão – que dirigia o veículo –, a mãe de 71 anos e outras duas passageiras.

O carro trafegava pela pista leste, sentido capital, quando o pneu dianteiro esquerdo estourou por volta das 19h40. O motorista perdeu o controle da direção e colidiu lateralmente com um veículo cinza.

Com o impacto, o automóvel capotou e Gilma foi projetada para fora do veículo. O corpo da vítima foi localizado a cerca de 50 metros do local do acidente.

Ainda segundo a polícia, dos outros ocupantes do carro em que a vítima estava, apenas uma passageira não sofreu ferimentos. O irmão da vítima, a mãe e a outra passageira tiveram escoriações leves e foram socorridos para hospitais da região.

No outro veículo, que era ocupado pelo motorista e mais três pessoas, incluindo duas crianças de 1 e 3 anos , não houve feridos.

No outro veículo, que era ocupado pelo motorista e mais três pessoas, não houve feridos — Foto: Portal CCM — ARTESP (ccm.artesp.sp.gov.br)

A Polícia Rodoviária realizou o teste do bafômetro nos motoristas dos dois veículos e o resultado foi negativo para ambos.

A ocorrência foi registrada como homicídio culposo (sem intenção de matar) e lesão corporal culposa na direção de veículo automotor. O caso será investigado para apurar se houve negligência.

articles.title: Homem é condenado por matar menina de 12 anos no PI | G1
articles.standfirst: José Carlos Oliveira da Silva foi condenado a 18 anos e 8 meses de prisão em Floriano.
articles.summary: José Carlos Oliveira da Silva foi condenado a 18 anos de prisão pela morte de Ester, de 12 anos, atingida por um tiro na cabeça a caminho da igreja em Floriano.
articles.body:
José Carlos Oliveira da Silva foi condenado a 18 anos e 8 meses de prisão por matar a adolescente Ester, de 12 anos, durante uma tentativa de homicídio em dezembro de 2025 , no bairro Catumbi, em Floriano, no Sul do Piauí.

O julgamento ocorreu no Tribunal do Júri. José Carlos foi condenado por homicídio qualificado, tentativa de homicídio e posse irregular de arma de fogo.

A menina seguia para uma atividade na igreja quando foi atingida por um tiro na cabeça. O disparo ocorreu durante um ataque contra José Nilton Fernandes de Carvalho, que passava pelo local quando José Carlos efetuou cerca de cinco tiros contra ele.

José Nilton também foi atingido, mas sobreviveu. A adolescente, que não tinha relação com o conflito, morreu ainda no local.

Durante o julgamento, o MP sustentou a condenação do réu por homicídio qualificado consumado, homicídio qualificado tentado, posse irregular de arma de fogo e corrupção de menores.

A acusação foi baseada no fato de que ele era transportado em uma motocicleta por uma adolescente que ainda não tinha 18 anos na época do crime .

O Conselho de Sentença, contudo, absolveu José Carlos dessa acusação, mas reconheceu a prática dos dois crimes contra a vida e da posse irregular de arma.

A sentença fixou pena de 16 anos de reclusão pelo homicídio qualificado da adolescente, além de 10 anos e 8 meses pela tentativa de homicídio contra José Nilton Fernandes de Carvalho .

Já pelo crime de posse irregular de arma de fogo, José Carlos recebeu pena de um ano de detenção, além do pagamento de 10 dias-multa.

Além da pena, a Justiça determinou o pagamento de indenização mínima de R$ 50 mil aos familiares de Ester e de R$ 5 mil à vítima que sobreviveu ao ataque.

Ester morreu após levar um tiro na cabeça na noite de quinta-feira (11) em Floriano — Foto: Reprodução

Uma menina de 12 anos, identificada, até o momento, apenas como Ester, morreu após levar um tiro na cabeça na noite do dia 11.12.2025 , no bairro Catumbi, em Floriano, Sul do Piauí. Ela seguia para uma atividade na igreja quando foi atingida durante um ataque a um homem.

Segundo a Polícia Militar, o alvo dos tiros era José Nilton Fernandes de Carvalho, conhecido como “Cabura”, de 32 anos. Ele passava pelo local quando dois criminosos chegaram em uma moto e atiraram. O homem usa tornozeleira eletrônica. A menina tentou correr, mas foi atingida na cabeça e morreu no local.

Imagens de câmeras de segurança mostram que os criminosos eram um homem e uma mulher. Ela pilotava a moto, enquanto ele desceu, se escondeu atrás de um carro e esperou o alvo. Quando viu José Nilton Fernandes de Carvalho, atirou várias vezes. A menina passava pela rua nesse momento e foi atingida.

O homem e a adolescente foram presos no 12.12.2025 em Floriano, no Sul do Piauí, suspeitos de participar do ataque a tiros que matou a menina Ester. A prisão foi confirmada pela Polícia Militar.

Segundo o 3º Batalhão da Polícia Militar, o casal foi encontrado em uma operação conjunta das polícias civil e militar.

Na época o homem confessou ter disparado os tiros, mas disse que o alvo era José Nilton Fernandes de 32 anos, que estava na rua no momento do crime.

articles.title: Motorista atira contra adega em Jundiaí após bater em carro e brigar | G1
articles.standfirst: Confusão começou na Avenida Francisco Nobre, no bairro Medeiros, no domingo (15); suspeito fugiu, mas carro usado por ele foi encontrado abandonado com munições dentro.
articles.summary: A polícia procura um homem que atirou contra uma adega e agrediu a proprietária no domingo (15), em Jundiaí (SP). Carro foi encontrado abandonado e com munições.
articles.body:
Caso foi registrado no Plantão Policial de Jundiaí (SP) — Foto: Google Maps/Reprodução

Um homem é procurado pela polícia após bater em um carro estacionado, agredir a dona de uma adega e efetuar disparos contra a fachada do comércio na noite de domingo (15), no bairro Medeiros, em Jundiaí (SP). Ninguém foi baleado.

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, a confusão começou às 20h15, na Avenida Francisco Nobre. O suspeito dirigia um carro preto e atingiu um automóvel que estava estacionado em frente ao estabelecimento. Ao ser avisado sobre a batida, o motorista desceu exaltado, negou ter atingido o veículo e iniciou uma discussão.

Durante o bate-boca, a proprietária da adega, de 24 anos, afirmou que o motorista estava errado e acabou sendo atingida no rosto por ele. O irmão dela, de 29 anos, tentou defendê-la e discutiu com o agressor. Outro homem, que se apresentou como irmão do motorista, também entrou na briga, que só terminou após a intervenção do dono do carro atingido, de 22 anos.

Após a confusão, o suspeito foi embora ameaçando voltar armado para matar os três. Alertadas por pessoas que estavam no local de que o homem realmente possuía uma arma de fogo, as vítimas deixaram a adega e se esconderam. Poucos minutos depois, ouviram diversos disparos. Os tiros atingiram e quebraram o vidro da fachada do estabelecimento.

Imagens de câmeras de segurança registraram o momento em que o suspeito atirou e, logo em seguida, outro homem tirou a arma das mãos dele e fugiu. Perto do comércio, os policiais recolheram uma munição intacta de calibre 38.

Durante buscas pela região, a Polícia Militar (PM) encontrou o carro usado pelo suspeito abandonado e trancado próximo ao cruzamento com a Avenida Juvenal Arantes. Pelo lado de fora, os policiais viram munições no interior do veículo, que foi apreendido e levado para um pátio em Várzea Paulista (SP) para passar por perícia.

As vítimas agredidas receberam requisição para exame de corpo de delito no Instituto Médico Legal (IML). O caso foi registrado como lesão corporal, disparo de arma de fogo, ameaça e dano no Plantão Policial e será investigado pelo 5º Distrito Policial de Jundiaí.

articles.title: New Zealand launches six-month graduate work visa today: Who among Indian students can apply?
articles.summary: New Zealand has opened applications for its new six-month Short-Term Graduate Work Visa from November 16, 2026, giving eligible international graduates,
articles.body: New Zealand has opened applications for its new six-month Short-Term Graduate Work Visa from November 16, 2026, giving eligible international graduates, including Indian students, an opportunity to stay and work in the country after completing their studies.Announced by Immigration New Zealand in September, the new visa is aimed at students who have completed eligible qualifications in New Zealand but do not meet the requirements for a Post-Study Work Visa. It allows graduates to work for any employer for up to six months while searching for employment and exploring longer-term work opportunities.Indian students who have completed a qualification at Level 5, 6 or 7 of the New Zealand Qualifications and Credentials Framework (NZQCF) can apply, subject to the immigration authority's eligibility requirements.To qualify, applicants must have studied full-time in New Zealand for a minimum of 24 weeks. Their qualification must not be in English language studies, foundation or bridging programmes. Micro-credentials are also excluded. Students whose qualifications make them eligible for a Post-Study Work Visa cannot apply under the new category.Three-month application deadlineOne of the key conditions is the application deadline. Graduates must apply within three months of the expiry of their student visa for the qualification on which their application is based. They must also have held a student visa for that qualification within the three months before applying.Applicants will need to demonstrate that they have at least NZD $5,000 in available funds to support themselves during their stay. They must meet New Zealand's health and character requirements and may be asked to submit medical certificates, chest X-rays or police certificates, depending on their circumstances.Students whose studies were funded under the Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship Programme must also obtain written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or Education New Zealand.What can graduates do under the new visa?The Short-Term Graduate Work Visa provides open work rights for six months. Holders can take up employment with any employer in New Zealand, provided the work is covered by an employment agreement or a contract for services.However, the visa does not permit holders to establish or operate a business as owners. It also does not allow them to provide commercial sexual services.The visa cannot be used to include a spouse or dependent children in the application. Holders can support visitor visa applications for their partners and dependent children. However, family members cannot obtain work or student visas solely on the basis of their relationship with the visa holder. Partners may apply for work visas independently, while dependent children can apply for student visas as international students.How to apply and what is the fee?Applications can be submitted online through Immigration New Zealand's Enhanced Immigration Online system (ADEPT), which opened for applications on November 16.Students must upload their qualification certificate, academic transcript or a letter from their education provider confirming completion of the programme or eligibility to graduate. They must also provide passport details, an acceptable photograph and evidence of sufficient funds.The visa fee starts at NZD $1,670. The final cost depends on the applicant's country and place of application.Can graduates extend their stay?Immigration New Zealand has specified that applicants can be granted only one Short-Term Graduate Work Visa. The six-month visa cannot be extended, and holders cannot apply for another visa under the same category.Those seeking to remain in New Zealand beyond the permitted period will need to obtain another visa before their current visa expires.Former Short-Term Graduate Work Visa holders can apply for another student visa only if their proposed programme is a bachelor's degree or a qualification at a higher NZQCF level than the one used for their graduate work visa, and the new qualification makes them eligible for a Post-Study Work Visa.Further information on eligibility, application requirements and visa conditions is available on Immigration New Zealand's official website: the latest Education News and Live updates. articles.title: 'It's acceptable to throw oneself into work...': Barack Obama challenges the idea of work-life balance; says success comes with trade-offs
articles.summary: The modern workplace sells a tidy promise called balance.
articles.body: The modern workplace sells a tidy promise called balance. Barack Obama, who held one of the most demanding jobs in the world for two terms, says the promise is incomplete at best.Speaking on The Pivot Podcast in 2024, the former president said excellence in any field, whether sports, music, business or politics, comes with seasons when a person is “out of balance” and “single-minded”. Anyone chasing a serious career goal, by his account, should expect long hours and working lunches.The price of a campaignObama learned this the hard way. When he first ran for president, he worked relentlessly for over a year and a half. Weekends offered some respite. Michelle Obama, who had a full-time job of her own, absorbed much of the domestic load, including the care of their daughters, Sasha and Malia.The effort led to two terms in the White House. It was also not sustainable, and Obama has said so himself.The 6:30 PM ruleAs president, he set a rule: dinner with his family every night at 6:30 PM, even if he returned to work afterwards. Some leaders might see that as lost time. Obama argued the opposite.“They ground you and give you perspective, and over time, that makes you better,” he said.At an Obama Foundation event in 2019, the former president was sharp about priorities. “I don’t think there’s a perfect formula,” he said, adding that on his deathbed he would not remember “any bill I passed” or “any speech I gave”.That is not a dismissal of ambition. He said the level of commitment a person can give to work depends on what life at home looks like, and the reverse holds too.A ledger, not a balance“There will be phases in your life where you have to prioritize different things,” Obama said. There are times, he said, when it is acceptable to throw oneself into work because everything at home is in a good place. There are other times when work must give way because things at home are not.The same logic applies to couples. When one partner chases a dream, the other covers the gap, and the favour must be returned. “You can have it all, but you can’t have it all at once,” he told The Pivot Podcast, referring to himself and Michelle. The aim, he said, is to “create some equity inside the family”.Balance, in Obama’s telling, is not a daily state to be achieved. It is a ledger kept over years. Debts are permitted, provided they are repaid.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Same cadre, different grade pay? Punjab and Haryana high court rejects Centre's plea, says MES employees appointed in July 2018 must get Rs 4,600 as others in the cadre continued to receive the upgraded pay
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: The Punjab and Haryana high court has dismissed a petition filed by the Union government challenging a tribunal order granting higher grade
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: The Punjab and Haryana high court has dismissed a petition filed by the Union government challenging a tribunal order granting higher grade pay to employees appointed as Supervisor Barrack and Store in the Military Engineering Service (MES), holding that similarly placed employees in the same cadre cannot be given different pay benefits.A division bench of Justice Harsimran Singh Sethi and Justice Minderjeet Yadav upheld the July 7, 2026, order of the Chandigarh bench of the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), which had directed the authorities to grant the employees grade pay of Rs 4,600 in Pay Band-2 instead of Rs 4,200.The court noted that the employees were appointed in July 2018, when the upgradation of the post from grade pay of Rs 4,200 to Rs 4,600 had already been approved by the President of India on December 15, 2017, and the benefit had been extended to other personnel in the cadre. The upgradation was subsequently kept in abeyance in October 2018.However, the bench held that this could not retrospectively deprive the employees of a benefit they were entitled to when appointed. "Once, on the date when they were appointed, the post was in the grade pay of Rs 4600 which benefit had already been extended to all the personnel working in such cadre, merely subsequent to the appointment that the upgradation of the post of Barrack and Store was kept in abeyance cannot be made applicable upon the respondents herein," the court observed. "Any order kept in abeyance can only be made applicable prospectively and not retrospectively," it added.The post of Supervisor Barrack and Store was advertised on January 6, 2015, with a prescribed pay scale of Rs 9,300-34,800 in Pay Band-2 and grade pay of Rs 4,200. Before the selection process was completed, a cadre review resulted in the post being upgraded to grade pay of Rs 4,600, with the President's approval communicated on December 15, 2017.While the revised benefit was extended to other personnel in the cadre, those appointed in July 2018 against the 2015 advertisement continued to receive grade pay of Rs 4,200. Their representations were rejected on May 9, 2019, following which they approached the CAT. "Once, even after keeping in abeyance the upgradation of pay-scale in the post of Supervisor Barrack and Store in October 2018, the benefit of upgradation already given to the employees is being continued to be enjoyed by them, arguing before this Court that such benefits should not have been given to the respondents, is incorrect," the bench observed.It said the tribunal's direction was valid and removed the anomaly of granting two different grade pays to similarly situated employees in the same cadre. The court also clarified that even if the original upgradation was beyond the authorities' jurisdiction, the government would have to withdraw the benefit from all employees receiving it, rather than selectively denying it to the petitioners.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: US universities oppose proposed $70,000 OPT fee: Could Indian students lose post-study work opportunities?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian students planning to pursue higher education in the United States could face uncertainty over post-study employment opportunities after
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian students planning to pursue higher education in the United States could face uncertainty over post-study employment opportunities after the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposed a fee of $70,000 for an initial Optional Practical Training (OPT) recommendation and $30,000 for subsequent recommendations.The proposal, published in the Federal Register on October 8, 2026, would require US colleges and universities to pay the specified amount when recommending eligible F-1 international students for OPT.The proposed charges have drawn opposition from the American Council on Education (ACE) and 36 other higher education organisations, which have called on the government to withdraw the plan.In a comment letter submitted to DHS on November 9, the organisations raised concerns that the proposed fees could place a substantial financial burden on universities and restrict international students' access to post-study employment opportunities.The proposal has not been finalised and the new charges are not currently in force. Students applying to US universities are therefore not required to pay these proposed amounts.What is OPT and why is it important for Indian students?Optional Practical Training is an employment authorisation programme available to eligible international students holding F-1 status in the US. It allows them to gain practical work experience related to their academic field during or after completing their studies.Under the existing rules, eligible international students can receive up to 12 months of standard OPT. Graduates with qualifying degrees in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) can apply for an additional 24-month extension.This means eligible STEM graduates can receive up to 36 months of practical training in total.OPT is an important consideration for Indian students choosing American universities, particularly those pursuing computer science, engineering, information technology and other professional programmes. It provides an opportunity to gain work experience in the US after graduation.However, OPT does not automatically lead to an H-1B visa or permanent residency. Graduates seeking to remain employed in the country beyond their authorised training period must qualify under another applicable immigration category.What are the proposed $70,000 and $30,000 fees?Under the DHS proposed fee structure, a Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP)-certified educational institution recommending an F-1 student for OPT would be required to pay an initial fee of $70,000.A subsequent recommendation for the same student would attract a fee of $30,000.The proposed fee structure distinguishes between the first and subsequent OPT recommendations. The initial charge would apply when an institution recommends a student for OPT for the first time, whether for pre-completion or post-completion training.The subsequent charge could apply to another period of OPT or a STEM OPT extension. However, a student changing employers would not, by itself, trigger another fee.The institution would have to pay the applicable amount before its designated school official enters the OPT recommendation in the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS).Importantly, the proposed payment obligation rests with the educational institution rather than the student. However, DHS has indicated that universities could determine the source of the funds, leaving open the possibility that institutions may seek to recover some of the cost through other arrangements.Why are universities opposing the proposed fee?The American Council on Education, along with 36 other higher education organisations, has urged DHS to withdraw the proposal.In their November 9 submission, the organisations argued that the proposed charges are substantially higher than the administrative costs involved in processing OPT recommendations.They also raised concerns about the financial implications for universities, particularly institutions with limited resources, and the possible impact on international student enrolment.According to ACE, OPT allows hundreds of thousands of international students on F-1 visas to gain practical experience in fields related to their academic qualifications. The proposed fees could make it financially difficult for universities to continue recommending students for the programme.The organisations have also warned that colleges and universities could become less willing to participate in OPT, potentially affecting the United States' ability to attract and retain international talent.Their submission called for the withdrawal of the proposal and a more realistic assessment of its economic impact, including the potential consequences for higher education institutions, international student enrolment and the wider US economy.These concerns form part of the higher education organisations' formal opposition to the proposal. DHS has not accepted their recommendations in the material provided.Could Indian students lose their post-study work opportunities?If implemented in its current form, the proposed fee structure could affect how universities approach OPT recommendations for international students.Institutions would have to consider the financial implications of paying $70,000 for an initial recommendation and $30,000 for a subsequent one. Some universities could absorb the cost, while others may explore alternative funding arrangements or reconsider their participation in the programme.The potential impact could be particularly significant for smaller institutions and universities operating with limited financial resources.For Indian students, the uncertainty concerns access to post-study employment opportunities rather than a direct increase in the OPT application fee payable to the government.However, the proposal does not mean that all universities will stop recommending students for OPT or that Indian graduates will automatically lose their eligibility. The actual impact will depend on the final rules and how individual institutions respond.The proposed charges are also not specific to Indian nationals. They would apply to eligible F-1 international students irrespective of nationality.What is the current status of the proposal?The DHS proposal was published in the Federal Register on October 8, 2026, under docket number ICEB-2026-0100. The general public-comment period closed on November 9, with ACE and 36 other higher education organisations submitting their objections on the final day.A separate deadline of December 7, 2026, applies to comments concerning the proposal's information-collection provisions under the Paperwork Reduction Act. This is not an extension of the general public-comment period on the proposed fees.As of November 16, 2026, the proposed fee structure has not been established as a final rule.Under the proposed implementation framework, the charges would apply prospectively to OPT recommendations made on or after the effective date of a final rule, with implementation beginning 60 days after its publication.For Indian students already studying in the US or planning to apply for upcoming university intakes, the existing OPT and STEM OPT provisions therefore remain relevant.The final outcome of the rulemaking process will determine whether the proposed charges are introduced, revised or withdrawn.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. articles.title: En 1972, se descubrió sin querer en Bulgaria el tesoro de oro más antiguo del mundo, del año 4.600 a.C.: se desenterraron tres mil objetos de oro
articles.standfirst: Un obrero dio por casualidad con un hallazgo que cambió la prehistoria europea.
articles.summary: Un obrero dio por casualidad con un hallazgo que cambió la prehistoria europea.
articles.body: Hay descubrimientos que llegan tras años de búsqueda y otros que aparecen por pura casualidad. El 22 de octubre de 1972, Raycho Marinov, un operador de excavadora de 22 años, abría una zanja cerca de la costa del mar Negro, en la ciudad búlgara de Varna, cuando su máquina sacó a la luz unos objetos extraños. Sin saber qué tenía entre manos, Marinov guardó algunas piezas en una caja de zapatos y se las llevó a casa. Unos días después avisó a los arqueólogos locales. Aquel gesto le valió una recompensa de 500 levas, el equivalente a varios sueldos de la época, y abrió la puerta a uno de los hallazgos más importantes de la prehistoria europea. Bajo la tierra se escondía un cementerio de la Edad del Cobre, hoy conocido como la necrópolis de Varna. Las excavaciones, dirigidas por Mihail Lazarov e Ivan Ivanov, se prolongaron durante casi dos décadas y sacaron a la luz cerca de 300 tumbas, 62 de ellas con objetos de oro. En total aparecieron más de 3.000 piezas, con un peso de unos seis kilos: collares, brazaletes, pendientes y pequeños discos que se cosían a la ropa. Datan de entre el 4.600 y el 4.200 a.C., lo que las convierte en el tesoro de oro trabajado más antiguo del mundo. La sepultura más espectacular es la número 43. Allí descansaba un hombre de más de 60 años rodeado de casi un tercio de todo el oro del yacimiento, entre ellos un cetro y una funda para el pene de oro. Esa sola tumba contenía más oro del que se ha encontrado en todo el resto del planeta para esa época. Para los expertos, el hallazgo demuestra que en Varna ya existía una sociedad jerarquizada, con líderes que se enterraban con riquezas extraordinarias, mucho antes que en Egipto o Mesopotamia. Hoy, la mayor parte del tesoro se expone en el Museo Arqueológico de Varna, y se calcula que todavía queda alrededor de un 30 % de la necrópolis por excavar.

articles.title: Inside one university's efforts to reclaim the classroom and fight antisemitism
articles.summary: Touro University's inaugural antisemitism symposium will feature Debra Messing, Gloria Gaynor and legal experts discussing practical ways to fight hate.
articles.body: As the rise in antisemitism continues, New York City's Touro University is convening its first symposium on antisemitism, bringing together legal experts, academics, policymakers and other leaders to discuss practical ways to fight hate. Monday's conference is expected to feature Touro University President Alan Kadish; Kenneth Marcus, founder of the Louis D. Brandeis Center for Human Rights Under Law; David Harris, former CEO of the American Jewish Committee; Touro law professor Mark Goldfeder; human rights scholar Anne Bayefsky; New York City Council speaker Julie Menin; actor Debra Messing and singer Gloria Gaynor, among others. It marks the first major public program for Touro University’s Antisemitism Institute. In addition to the distinguished guests, the program will include the release of new research and discussions on interventions to fight hate, including a newly launched Touro University Teaching Fellowship to Combat Campus Antisemitism. The fellowship, which is held under the school's Antisemitism Institute, in association with National Jewish Advocacy Center (NJAC), is designed to help professors teach courses within their academic specialties that shed light on antisemitism. JEWISH CAMPUS LIFE AT A ‘CROSSING POINT’ AS STUDENTS WEIGH ANTISEMITISM RISKS, NEW REPORT SHOWS "What is missing is a program that is directed at the people that are in the front lines, faculty, administration, people that in the educational front line, and they are craving to have the tools to intervene," Ido Aharoni, the symposium host, a former Israeli diplomat and global distinguished professor of business at Touro University, told Fox News Digital. Aharoni explained that rather than focusing on the origins of anti-Jewish hatred, the symposium aims to bring great minds from different industries together to discuss how to combat it. This message was echoed by Kadish, who told Fox News Digital that "we're not focused just on categorizing antisemitism. We want to see what we can do to combat antisemitism and hate." He said that the majority of the university's activities were "designed to create a better future." Kadish told Fox News Digital that as the university recognized rising instances of antisemitism in New York, and around the country, the idea for the Antisemitism Institute was formed. The institute officially launched in the spring of 2026 and the first faculty cohort of its fellowship met in August. "The idea was to do things, not to replicate what other people are doing, but to do things that were unique because we're a university, and we're a university under Jewish auspices. So, we felt that it was our obligation to try to do what we could to fight antisemitism," Kadish told Fox News Digital. JEWISH STUDENT SUES NEW YORK SCHOOL ON OCT 7 ANNIVERSARY OVER 'RELENTLESS ANTISEMITIC HARASSMENT' The Antisemitism Institute is designed to partner with professors across the country to disseminate research, study legal tools, evaluate the need for legislation, examine the role of social media in the spread of antisemitism and train the next generation of attorneys to handle cases in the field. Kadish said that following the Oct. 7 attacks in Israel, there has been "a tsunami of hatred, bias and racism." He added that there were two clear factors at play: increased acceptance of antisemitic rhetoric and the rise of online bots driving the conversation. Rabbi Mark Goldfeder, Esq., who leads the Antisemitism Institute fellowship and serves as the CEO and director of NJAC, said that partnering with professors was key to changing minds, not only on campus, but in the broader society. He emphasized the importance of treating the university classroom as "one of the most powerful rooms in the West," as activists, according to him, had been doing for decades. "The university classroom is where the West decides what it believes. And for about two, maybe three decades now, on the subject of Jews, it had been deciding wrong and largely uncontested," Goldfeder told Fox News Digital. Goldfeder argued that the post-Oct. 7 rise in antisemitism on college campuses was not a spur-of-the-moment spike in hate, but rather the result of something that had been brewing for years. POLITICAL ACTIVISM, ANTISEMITISM ALLEGATIONS PUT PUBLIC SCHOOLS UNDER THE MICROSCOPE "The campus eruptions after Oct. 7 weren't spontaneous, right? Somebody assigned the readings, somebody framed the questions, somebody graded the papers for years, and a lot of the students, you know, in those tents, for example, they didn't know which river or which sea they were chanting about, but they were there because someone that they trusted — often a professor, a teacher — had given them a story that was simple and broad enough to explain the whole world for them," he told Fox News Digital. For the fellowship, the university brought in 10 professors from 10 different campuses with a variety of religious backgrounds to teach them how to lead courses in their disciplines while including antisemitism education. Goldfeder told Fox News Digital that the courses are not meant to be "one-sided sermons" and include sophisticated, strong opposing arguments. "What we are trying to do is teach people how to think. The goal is not to replace one orthodoxy with another, but to restore a sort of basic academic rule, which is that claims require evidence," he said. Touro estimates that the first cycle of its fellowship could reach approximately 1,000 students, as the professors are committed to teaching the course at least twice, according to Kadish. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE The university's efforts go beyond higher education, as the Antisemitism Institute includes an Antisemitism Law Clinic, which Goldfeder leads. The clinic aims to train law students to respond to antisemitism through existing civil rights laws. This becomes crucial as freedom of speech concerns are often raised in cases of campus antisemitism. Goldfeder told Fox News Digital that universities must distinguish what constitutes protected speech versus harassment. "A checkpoint is not speech. Preventing a person from entering the classroom is not speech. Targeted harassment is not speech. Most of what you're seeing on campus is protected speech, but much, much of the stuff you're seeing in the news is not protected speech. And we have to be very, very careful not to sweep both of those with the same brush," Goldfeder told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Those efforts will be among the topics discussed at Touro's inaugural symposium on antisemitism, which has sessions on antisemitism in academia, new research on the spread of antisemitism, the relationship between anti-Zionism and antisemitism and training current and future leaders. "We're not going to solve the problem single-handedly, obviously, but at least we believe that we can make a difference," Aharoni said.

articles.title: Joana Sanz estalla contra Dani Alves tras su ruptura: "Gasté mi dinero en pagar tus cuentas y tus deudas"
articles.standfirst: La modelo ha respondido públicamente a un mensaje del exfutbolista en el que aseguraba que Jesús fue el único que permaneció a su lado durante sus momentos más difíciles
articles.summary: La modelo ha respondido públicamente a un mensaje del exfutbolista en el que aseguraba que Jesús fue el único que permaneció a su lado durante sus momentos más difíciles
articles.body: Joana Sanz ha respondido con dureza a Dani Alves después de que el exfutbolista publicara un mensaje en el que hablaba de su conversión religiosa y aseguraba que, durante su etapa más complicada, cuando otras personas le dieron la espalda, Jesús permaneció a su lado. La modelo ha utilizado los comentarios de esa publicación para recordar el apoyo que, según asegura, prestó a quien entonces era su marido durante su estancia en prisión y reprocharle que haya omitido su presencia en ese relato. "Menudo descaro el tuyo de decir públicamente que solo se quedó Jesús", comienza el extenso comentario que Sanz ha escrito en redes sociales. La modelo sostiene que mantuvo su dolor en un segundo plano porque consideraba que Alves estaba atravesando una situación todavía peor y que no quiso negarle el apoyo emocional que necesitaba. "Me quedé con mi dolor reprimido porque consideré que tú estabas en peor situación y no era capaz de negarte ese aliento de calma que te daba el coger tus llamadas", explica. A continuación, enumera algunos de los gestos que asegura haber tenido con el exjugador durante aquellos meses: las visitas a prisión, el acompañamiento en fechas señaladas y la ayuda económica. "Te visité a pesar de caerme encima el mundo entero y tener que lidiar con el foco mediático de titulares que no me correspondían. Te acompañé en Navidad pudiendo pasarla con mi familia", relata. Una de las acusaciones más contundentes llega cuando se refiere al dinero que habría destinado a ayudarle: "Gasté MI DINERO en pagar tus cuentas y tus deudas". La reacción de Sanz llega después de que Alves compartiera un testimonio religioso en el que repasaba su experiencia personal y su acercamiento a la fe durante su paso por prisión. El mensaje fue difundido a través de una publicación de una cuenta vinculada a un ministerio de adoración y posteriormente compartido en sus redes. "Hubo amigos que se fueron. Personas en las que confié que me dieron la espalda cuando más las necesitaba. Pero cuando todos se alejaron, Jesús permaneció", afirmaba el exfutbolista. En el mismo texto aseguraba que había encontrado en su fe el apoyo que no había recibido de otras personas: "Cuando otros me abandonaron, él me sostuvo. Cuando otros dudaron de mí, él siguió conmigo". Es precisamente esa afirmación la que ha provocado el reproche público de su expareja. Sanz sostiene que estuvo a su lado durante ese periodo pese a las consecuencias personales y mediáticas que tuvo para ella. También asegura que Alves llegó a decirle que se buscara la vida sola y que fue él quien la apartó. "Tú me echaste y yo me quité para ponerte a ti cuando eras la última persona del planeta que deberías de haber recibido apoyo o bondad", escribe. La modelo añade que otras personas del entorno del exfutbolista sí le dieron la espalda, mientras que ella continuó visitándolo y ayudándolo. El comentario termina con una nueva crítica a la actitud de Alves: "A mí, que ni un vuelo me tuviste que sacar para visitarte jamás en la vida, me pagas con mal agradecimiento de manera pública. Tardé en darme cuenta, pero mejor tarde que nunca". La respuesta llega apenas unos días después de que trascendiera la separación de la pareja, que se casó en 2017. Joana Sanz confirmó el distanciamiento a través de Instagram y, posteriormente, explicó al periodista Javi Hoyos que la nueva vida religiosa de Alves había contribuido a alejarles. Según esa información, la modelo ya habría iniciado los trámites de divorcio. El exfutbolista, que pasó 14 meses en prisión preventiva después de ser acusado de una agresión sexual en una discoteca de Barcelona, fue condenado en febrero de 2024 a cuatro años y seis meses de cárcel. Sin embargo, el Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Cataluña revocó la condena en marzo de 2025 y lo absolvió al considerar que la sentencia no había valorado adecuadamente determinadas pruebas y que existían dudas sobre la fiabilidad del testimonio de la denunciante.

articles.title: Supreme Court declines Trump administration’s DEI research grant appeal
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday declined to hear an appeal from the Trump administration in its bid to terminate tens of millions of dollars in research grants to higher education institutions in California as part of its push against diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) initiatives. The justices indicated they would not take the case in…
articles.body:
The Supreme Court on Monday declined to hear an appeal from the Trump administration in its bid to terminate tens of millions of dollars in research grants to higher education institutions in California as part of its push against diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) initiatives.

The justices indicated they would not take the case in a one-line order that did not include any explanation. There were no noted dissents.

The Trump administration had asked the court to review a May decision from a 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals panel that upheld a preliminary injunction blocking the cancellation of certain grants within the University of California (UC) system based on executive orders targeting DEI practices.

The appeals court held that terminating the grants was “aimed at the suppression of viewpoints with which the government disagrees” and likely violated the First Amendment.

The Justice Department contends that the federal government has “significant discretion” in determining how taxpayer funds are used and argued the Constitution does not bar the government from declining to fund research projects that promote ideologies it opposes.

“The general requirement of viewpoint neutrality does not require taxpayers to continue funding projects that the government concludes no longer serve the public interest, even if that conclusion is based in part on the viewpoint furthered by the projects,” Solicitor General D. John Sauer wrote in a petition to the court.

The funding cuts were initially challenged in June 2025 after a group of UC researchers who had received multiyear research grants from three federal agencies were informed the funding would be abruptly cut pursuant to several of President Trump’s executive orders.

Lawyers for the researchers described the cuts as a “devastating blow,” warning they could lead to lab closures, staff layoffs and stalled research. They urged the justices not to take the case.

“Those receiving grants have justifiably relied on them and, as found by the lower courts in this case, suffer enormous harm when the funding is suddenly terminated,” they wrote to the justices. “What begins as material harm — loss of money, staff, graduate and post-doctoral students — quickly becomes expressive harm: the inability to publish research and affect public discourse. This is a quintessential First Amendment violation.”

Trump made dismantling DEI programs a central focus in the early months of his second term, issuing several executive orders within the first weeks of his term to eliminate diversity initiatives across federal agencies, the military and other federally funded institutions.

articles.title: After the blue wave, what happens to education policy and parental rights protections in flipped states?
articles.summary: Democratic governors in previously red states look to target school vouchers and change education policies as they come to power next year.
articles.body: Democrats' sweeping midterm victories in several key governor's races could usher in a new era for education policy, raising urgent questions about the future of the parental rights laws Republicans spent years cementing after the COVID-19 pandemic. While incoming Democratic governors in states like Ohio, Iowa, Georgia and Texas are unlikely to dismantle every parental notification or curriculum transparency law overnight, education battles in those states are poised to shift sharply — particularly around school choice, state takeovers, and public school funding. Since the pandemic, contentious school board meetings have fueled a nationwide movement of parents demanding greater oversight of classroom instruction and challenging sexually explicit or LGBTQ-related books in school libraries. DEMOCRATS SEIZE MAJORITY OF GOVERNORS’ OFFICES IN ELECTION-NIGHT SHIFT Conservative groups capitalized on that momentum. Beginning in 2022, the Virginia-based American Principles Project (APP) entered local school board races in Florida, airing attack ads criticizing critical race theory and gender ideology. Alongside groups like the 1776 Project PAC, APP helped conservatives flip school board seats across Florida after Gov. Ron DeSantis broke precedent by actively endorsing local school board candidates who backed his pro-parent agenda. Republican governors soon followed up with statewide legislation establishing "Parents' Bills of Rights" and curriculum transparency mandates: FLORIDA'S DESANTIS DESCRIBES GOP MIDTERMS WIPEOUT AS 'CLOSE TO AN EXTINCTION-LEVEL EVENT' FOR REPUBLICANS DEPT OF ED PUSHES AHEAD WITH EFFORTS TO DISMANTLE FEDERAL BUREAUCRACY AFTER BLUE WAVE Now, voters in those four states have elected Democratic governors: Amy Acton in Ohio, Rob Sand in Iowa, Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia and Gina Hinojosa in Texas. Even if those incoming governors want to roll back existing parental rights laws, several will face steep legislative hurdles. Acton, Sand and Bottoms will still contend with Republican-controlled legislatures capable of blocking repeals, though Democrats made legislative gains in Texas and Georgia during the midterms. Notably, none of the four governors-elect campaigned explicitly on repealing their states' Parents' Bills of Rights. Instead, they largely sidestepped cultural flashpoints in favor of attacking GOP-backed private school voucher programs and calling for increased public school funding. DEMOCRATS COULD CREATE 'ANGRY' 'SINGLE-ISSUE' VOTERS IN 2028 IF THEY REMOVE SCHOOL CHOICE, CEO WARNS "This is a victory for the parents of Texas. We are taking our children’s education back from a government that has failed them," Hinojosa told supporters. "Schools will not be taken out of our control. They will not be shuttered or suffocated... On day one, I will fire [Texas Education Agency Commissioner] Mike Morath, and we will work tirelessly to repair the damage of the Texas voucher scam, and end an era in which our schools are sold for parts." Their pushback comes as major urban districts navigate shifting enrollment dynamics. In February, for example, the Houston Independent School District's state-appointed board voted unanimously to close or consolidate 12 campuses ahead of the 2026–2027 school year, citing enrollment declines alongside the state's expanding school choice framework. Still, conservatives warn that Hinojosa's legislative record signals a threat to parental protections in Texas. During the campaign, Abbott's team ran ads featuring Moms for Liberty activist Denise Bell arguing that Hinojosa's policies would undermine parents and jeopardize fairness in girls' sports. "Gina Hinojosa voted in favor of schools transitioning students behind parents’ backs, for sex change surgeries for kids, and for boys competing in girls’ sports—all radical policies that Governor Abbott has fought against time and again," Abbott’s campaign said in a statement accompanying the ad. "Parents should be the primary decision makers in their children’s lives." Meanwhile, the Trump administration is signaling it will use federal leverage to keep parental rights policies intact regardless of statehouse flips. Last year, President Donald Trump signed executive orders tying federal education funding to strict anti-discrimination compliance and prohibiting diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) programs in schools. Following the midterm results, the U.S. Department of Education told Fox News Digital it plans to escalate enforcement — including investigating school districts accused of concealing a student's gender transition from parents. "The Department will double down on its efforts to restore parental rights, return education to the states, and open more higher education pathways for students," an Education Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital. TEXAS DEMOCRATS PUT DEI BACK ON AGENDA AFTER SWEEPING TO POWER Defending Education, which has been the tip of the spear of the parental rights movement, investigating civil rights violations and exposing far-left elements of curriculum across the country, told Fox News Digital that the federal government already has strong laws, like FERPA and the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (PPRA), to protect parental rights. "These give the administration solid footing to make sure parents aren’t being kept in the dark about what’s happening at school, can review curriculum, and can opt out of invasive surveys on topics like gender ideology," said Paul Runko, senior director of strategic initiatives at Defending Education. He added: "The Justice Department has also stepped up, using investigations and lawsuits to push back against state and local school boards that cross the line." Runko explained further that civil rights protections would allow parents to continue to speak out in public forums. "On top of that, the First and 14th Amendments protect a parent’s right to speak up and decide how to raise their children. Recent federal court wins by parents in Ohio, Maryland and California send a clear message that school districts should think twice about ignoring parental rights," he said. None of the newly elected governors responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: Condenan a Luis Lorenzo a cinco años y tres meses de cárcel y a su expareja a nueve años de prisión por retener y vejar a la tía de ella
articles.standfirst: La Audiencia Provincial de Madrid considera probado que ambos aislaron a la anciana, de 85 años, le impidieron regresar a su casa en Asturias y la sometieron a un trato degradante
articles.summary: La Audiencia Provincial de Madrid considera probado que ambos aislaron a la anciana, de 85 años, le impidieron regresar a su casa en Asturias y la sometieron a un trato degradante
articles.body: La Audiencia Provincial de Madrid ha condenado al actor Luis Lorenzo a cinco años y tres meses de prisión y a su expareja, Aránzazu Suárez, a nueve años y un día de cárcel, por los delitos cometidos contra la tía de esta última, Isabel Suárez, una mujer de 85 años que falleció en 2021. El tribunal considera probado que ambos la aislaron de sus familiares, le impidieron regresar a su domicilio en Asturias y la sometieron a un trato degradante, anulando su libertad de movimientos. La sentencia, dictada por la Sección 29 de la Audiencia Provincial de Madrid, impone a Luis Lorenzo cuatro años de prisión por un delito de detención ilegal y 15 meses por trato degradante. En el caso de Aránzazu Suárez, la condena asciende a nueve años y un día: cuatro años por detención ilegal, tres años y seis meses por estafa agravada continuada y 18 meses por un delito contra la integridad moral. Los hechos se remontan al 10 de marzo de 2021, cuando la pareja acudió al domicilio de Isabel en Grado, en Asturias, y la convenció para trasladarse temporalmente a su vivienda de Rivas-Vaciamadrid. La mujer pensaba que permanecería allí unos días, como había sucedido en otras ocasiones, y que después regresaría a su casa. Sin embargo, nunca volvió a Asturias y permaneció en Madrid hasta su fallecimiento. Según los hechos probados, los acusados actuaron de común acuerdo para aislar a la anciana de sus hermanos, cuñadas, sobrinas y amigos, dificultando sus comunicaciones telefónicas y evitando que pudiera regresar a su entorno habitual, pese a que ese era su deseo. Antes del traslado, Isabel llevaba una vida autónoma: se desplazaba sola en tren, acudía al mercado y realizaba sus tareas cotidianas sin ayuda. Durante los meses que permaneció en Madrid, sin embargo, fue perdiendo progresivamente movilidad y facultades cognitivas hasta encontrarse en una situación de gran dependencia y vulnerabilidad. La resolución considera acreditado que no recibió los cuidados que necesitaba, no se le administraba correctamente la medicación prescrita y dormía en una cama inadecuada. También señala que los acusados le impedían utilizar los cuartos de baño de la vivienda y la obligaban a bajar a los aseos comunes del garaje. Uno de los episodios recogidos en la sentencia ocurrió el 17 de abril de 2021, cuando Luis Lorenzo y Aránzazu Suárez acudieron al parque temático Warner para celebrar el cumpleaños de uno de sus hijos y dejaron a Isabel sola durante unas ocho horas en un restaurante de un centro comercial de Rivas-Vaciamadrid. Lo hicieron pese a conocer las limitaciones cognitivas que ya presentaba y, según el tribunal, desatendiendo las llamadas de los trabajadores del establecimiento y de la Policía Municipal. Los magistrados consideran que estas circunstancias, junto con las restricciones impuestas a su vida cotidiana y el aislamiento de sus seres queridos, constituyeron un ataque a la integridad moral y a la dignidad de la anciana. La Audiencia también considera probado que Aránzazu Suárez se aprovechó del deterioro cognitivo y de la situación de dependencia de su tía para obtener un beneficio económico. En concreto, el 7 de mayo de 2021, después de que Isabel permaneciera ingresada en urgencias en el Hospital Ramón y Cajal de Madrid, su sobrina la acompañó a una notaría, donde otorgó un nuevo testamento a su favor y revocó el anterior. El documento le atribuía la vivienda que la anciana tenía en Grado y las cantidades depositadas en sus cuentas bancarias. El tribunal concluye que Isabel carecía entonces de libertad para testar y del conocimiento suficiente para otorgar válidamente esa disposición. Por ello, declara nulo el testamento y obliga a Aránzazu Suárez a devolver 15.097,50 euros a la masa hereditaria, más los intereses legales correspondientes. La resolución absuelve a Aránzazu Suárez de los delitos de maltrato habitual y administración desleal continuada. Por su parte, Luis Lorenzo queda absuelto de estafa agravada y administración desleal, además del delito de maltrato habitual. También queda absuelta de todos los delitos que se le imputaban Ana Elizabeth V., la cuidadora de Isabel. Los magistrados consideran que no existen pruebas suficientes para atribuirle el trato degradante o el maltrato habitual. Por el contrario, las conversaciones que mantuvo con la empresa para la que trabajaba reflejan su preocupación por el estado de la anciana y sus avisos sobre la falta de medicación y de material necesario para atenderla. La sentencia no es firme y contra ella cabe interponer recurso de apelación ante la Sala de lo Civil y Penal del Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Madrid.
